findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed the sanitizer buckets (quat) were testing below an effective concentration (100ppm) instead of between 200-400ppm. The triple sink hose was also testing at 100ppm. CORRECTED: PIC confirmed that the bag of sanitizer was not empty. PIC then switched out the green nozzle attachment at the dispenser which controls how much sanitizer that is mixed with water. Sanitizing solution then tested at 200pm, which was then used to refill the sanitizer buckets. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are always testing at an effective concentration, between 200-400ppm. Results of sanitizer testing should be read within several seconds of testing.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
THIS IS A SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed that not all employees have food handler certificates. The PIC was reminded that all employees who do not have Certified Food Protection Manager certificates must obtain training in basic food handling principles within 30 days of employment. Ensure that all required employees have food handler certificates by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

findings.comment: Observed the sanitizer buckets were testing at less than 100 ppm (quat) when the inspector arrived. Upon checking the sanitizer dispenser at the triple sink the PIC noticed that the sanitizer bag was empty. The PIC switched the empty bag with a full one and filled new sanitzier buckets that tested at 200 ppm (quat). The inspector educated that sanitizing solutions should be checked on a regular basis. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are always testing at the correct concentration.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The employee was educated when the action was observed. The PIC was instructed to remind all employees about the proper hand washing procedure. Ensure that a barrier is always used to turn off the faucet after hand washing to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: Observed a personal cell phone and speaker stored on a dish drying rack above the triple sink leaning against a clean bucket used for washing produce. The employee removed the phone from the location and placed it into a designated personal storage area. The bucket was also washed, rinsed, and sanitized during the inspection. Ensure that personal items are kept in designated areas to avoid contamination.
findings.citation_text: 6-403.11(B) Designated Areas. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES can not occur.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: The sanitizer buckets in the facility were observed to test at 100ppm of Quaternary ammonium. CORRECTED- The buckets were remade and tested to be at 200ppm of Quat. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are routinely tested and changed if not at the recommended concentration of 200 to 400ppm of Quaternary ammonium. 

Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Observed there was no paper towels at the front hand-washing sink. The PIC replaced the empty paper towel dispenser at the front hand-sink during the inspection. Ensure there are always paper-towels available at every hand-sink.

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: Observed raw meats stored above beans in the left standing cooler. The PIC moved the raw meat below the beans during the inspection. Ensure that food is always kept in its correct storage order to prevent cross contamination.

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Observed sanitizer buckets testing at 100 ppm (QUAT). Upon further investigation, it was found that the sanitizer at the triple sink used to fill the sanitizer buckets was almost empty. The PIC replaced the sanitizer and dumped & refilled the sanitizer buckets. The buckets were then testing at 200 ppm. Ensure that sanitizer is tested on a regular basis and meets the proper criteria. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label (200-400ppm), and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D)

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-201.11: Observed there was a spray bottle of sanitizer stored on a shelf above bags of chips. The PIC moved the spray bottle off the shelf and away from the chips during the inspection. Ensure chemicals are stored away or above food and food-contact surfaces to prevent contamination.

7-201.11: (A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below).

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204.112: Observed there are hanging thermometers missing from the standing coolers. Ensure that every refrigerated food storage unit has a temperature measuring device to measure air temperature.

4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-502.11: Observed a rubber spatula missing pieces at the food contact end. The PIC threw out the spatula during the inspection. Ensure all utensils are maintained in good repair. 

4-502.11: (A) UTENSILS shall be maintained in a state of repair or condition that complies with the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2 or shall be discarded. (C) Ambient air temperature, water pressure, and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be maintained in good repair and be accurate within the intended range of use.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: Observed that the back hand-sink by the dish area had a gap between the splash guard and the sink. Ensure the gap is sealed to maintain physical facilities in good repair.

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-303.11: Observed there is a lightbulb missing over the prep table. Ensure there is adequate lighting in food prep areas.

6-303.11: The light intensity shall be at least a certain lux and present in certain areas.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed that not all the food handler certificates are in the binder in the manager’s office. The PIC could not find the food handler certification for any employees currently working in the facility. Ensure employees complete food handler training within 30 days of hire, and that copies of all food handler certificates are kept at the facility.

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
Inspector observed that the drain for the triple sink is not draining during the inspection. The drain is full of water and has reached the lower edge of the air gapped drain pipe from the triple sink. Ensure that the drain is functioning properly at all times to allow for the proper disposal waste water to the sanitary sewer system. Upon asking an employee why the drain was backing up, the sock filter on the drain was pulled and the water drained properly. Discussed with person-in-charge the need to ensure that the drain is draining properly at all times to prevent any backup of waste water into the facility. The violation has been corrected and no follow-up is required at this time.

5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Upon arrival to the facility, inspector observed an employee at the register who needed assistance with the processing of a consumer debit/credit card. The person-in-charge assisted the employee with the process but was observed to return to food service/preparation immediately after touching the debit/credit card without switching gloves and washing hands. Ensure that hands are washed between activities that may have contaminated the hands/gloves. Discuss with employees the need to wash hands between such activities. Inspector immediately instructor person-in-charge to wash hands before returning to food service. Person-in-charge washed hands immediately. Corrected on site. 

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a wet wiping cloth on the counter immediately to the east of the drive-thru window. Wet wiping cloths must be stored in sanitizer solution at all times when not actively being used to wipe surfaces and may not be stored on countertops or other surfaces. Ensure that all employees are aware that wet wiping cloths must be stored in sanitizer solution (buckets) between uses. The wiping cloth was removed from the counter immediately and placed in sanitizer solution. Corrected on site. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.
